subject: physics
title: Gas temperature, pressure and absolute zero
key_idea: Gas particles move randomly and collide with the walls of their container. Heating a gas makes the particles faster, so the pressure rises if the volume is fixed. **Absolute zero** is 0 K, which is −273 °C.

blocks.text: This section covers how the motion of gas particles produces the pressure of a gas.

items: The particles in a gas are in constant random motion.
They move in random directions.
They move with a range of speeds.
The temperature of the gas is related to the average kinetic energy of the particles.

items.meaning: The force the gas particles exert on a surface, for every unit of area.

blocks.text: How a gas exerts a pressure

items: Gas particles collide with the walls of the container.
Each collision exerts a force on the wall.
Many collisions every second give a steady pressure on the wall.
Gas particles move randomly, with a range of speeds.
Temperature is related to the average kinetic energy of the particles.
Pressure is caused by particles colliding with the walls and exerting a force.

sections.heading: Temperature and pressure at constant volume

blocks.text: Here the mass of gas and the volume of the container stay fixed. Only the temperature changes.

diagram.alt: A cold gas and a hot gas in the same sealed container, compared by particle speed, collisions, force and pressure.
items: Cold gas
Hot gas

rows.feature: Collisions with the walls each second

items: Heating raises the average kinetic energy, so the particles move faster.
They hit the walls more often.
They hit the walls with more force each time.
A greater force on the same area means a greater pressure.

blocks.text: Cooling does the reverse. The particles are slower, so the pressure decreases. Learn this as a qualitative link only.

items: Higher temperature means faster particles with more kinetic energy.
They collide with the walls more often and with greater force.
So the pressure of a fixed volume of gas increases. Cooling decreases it.

sections.heading: Absolute zero and the kelvin scale

blocks.text: As a gas cools, its particles slow down. There is a lowest possible temperature.

items.meaning: The lowest possible temperature, 0 K or −273 °C, where the particles have no movement.
A temperature scale that starts at absolute zero. A change of 1 K is the same as a change of 1 °C.

items: To go from kelvin to Celsius, subtract 273.
A temperature in kelvin is never negative.
For example, 660 °C is 660 + 273 = 933 K.

items: Absolute zero is −273 °C, which is 0 K.
Add 273 to go from °C to K. Subtract 273 to go from K to °C.
Kelvin temperatures are never negative.

checks.q: Explain how gas particles exert a pressure on the walls of a container.
checks.a: The particles are in constant random motion and collide with the walls. Each collision exerts a force on the wall.

checks.q: A sealed container of gas is heated. The volume does not change. Explain why the pressure increases.
checks.a: The particles have a greater average kinetic energy (they move faster). They collide with the walls more often and with greater force. A greater force on the same area gives a greater pressure.

checks.q: Convert 27 °C to kelvin. Then state what is meant by absolute zero.
checks.a: 27 + 273 = 300 K. Absolute zero is −273 °C (0 K), where the particles have no movement.

exam_phrases: particles have a higher (mean) kinetic energy
particles move with greater speeds (on average)
more collisions with the walls per second
greater forces exerted in collisions
greater force exerted on the same area
the particles move in random directions
the particles move with a range of speeds

mistakes.wrong: At a higher temperature the particles vibrate more, so the pressure increases.
mistakes.right: Vibrate and vibrations are not accepted for a gas. Say the particles have a higher mean kinetic energy or move faster.

mistakes.wrong: The gas is hotter, so the pressure goes up.
mistakes.right: Explain it with particles: higher kinetic energy, more frequent collisions with the walls and a greater force. The pressure mark needs at least one other mark.

mistakes.wrong: All the particles in a gas move at the same speed.
mistakes.right: The particles move in random directions and with a range of speeds.

worked_example.question: The temperature of the helium in a balloon was increased. The mass and volume of helium in the balloon remained constant. Explain why the pressure exerted by the helium inside the balloon would increase.
answer_points: The particles have a higher (mean) kinetic energy (they move faster).
There is an increased number of collisions with the walls of the balloon per second.
There are greater forces exerted in the collisions between the particles and the balloon walls.
There is a greater force exerted on the same area.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each step. Do not accept that the particles vibrate more.

exam_phrases: gas particles are continually in motion
collide / hit / bombard the sides (walls) of the container
(gas particles) exert a force on the side of the container
particles move faster at a higher temperature
greater velocity / speed means greater kinetic energy
particles hit the container more frequently
bigger pressure because p = F / A

mistakes.wrong: The melting point of aluminium is 660 °C, which is −933 K.
mistakes.right: Add 273: 660 + 273 = 933 K. A negative value is not accepted.
Add 273 to a Celsius temperature: −4 + 273 = 269 K.

mistakes.wrong: When the gas is heated, the pressure is higher.
mistakes.right: This is only an isolated idea. Link it: faster particles have more kinetic energy, hit the walls more often and with more force, so p = F / A is larger.

worked_example.question: A fixed mass of gas is inside a cylinder with a movable piston. Describe, in terms of gas particles, how the gas exerts a pressure on the cylinder.
answer_points: The gas particles are continually in motion.
They collide with (hit or bombard) the sides of the container.
The gas particles exert a force on the side of the container.
worked_example.tip: Any three of these four points score the three marks.

exam_phrases: higher (average) speed / more (kinetic) energy
collide more frequently / often with the walls of the container
bigger force (over the same area) equals greater pressure
the mass of the air stays the same
the speed of the air molecules decreases
the pressure exerted by the air decreases

mistakes.wrong: Temperature affects the speed of the particles, which affects the pressure.
mistakes.right: The direction of the temperature change must be clear. For an increase in temperature, the particles have a higher average speed and the pressure increases.

mistakes.wrong: When warm air in a sealed bottle is put in icy water, the mass of the air decreases.
mistakes.right: The mass of the air stays the same. The speed of the molecules, the force on the walls and the pressure all decrease.

mistakes.wrong: The molecules hit the walls with a bigger force, so the pressure is greater.
mistakes.right: Link the force to the area: a bigger force over the same area equals a greater pressure.

worked_example.question: A student investigates a gas at constant volume. Explain, using ideas about particles, how temperature affects gas pressure.
answer_points: For an increase in temperature, the gas particles have a higher average speed (more kinetic energy).
They collide more frequently with the walls of the container.
A bigger force over the same area gives a greater pressure.
worked_example.tip: State the direction of the temperature change. The reverse argument for a decrease in temperature is also credited.
